tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

def publish_people(runs_dir: str | Path, data: dict, catalog, area: StudyArea, out_dir: str | Path) -> int:
    """people.parquet: the main run's synthetic persons for the map's people layer, each
    with an E911 address point, exact age and poverty ratio, catalog categories and a
    fixed uniform draw `u`.
    A data point marks a person a case when u < their risk, so changing a model only
    adds or removes cases at the margin instead of reshuffling who has it."""
    p = people_frame(pd.read_parquet(Path(runs_dir) / "main" / "persons.parquet"), data, catalog, area)
    p.drop(columns=["seed_serial", "seed_person"]).to_parquet(Path(out_dir) / "people.parquet", index=False)
    return len(p)


def people_frame(persons: pd.DataFrame, data: dict, catalog, area: StudyArea) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One run's persons as the people layer shows them, in person_id order: IDs, parcel
    and block, a map point, exact age and poverty ratio, catalog categories and `u`.
    Every run uses the same random streams, so the main run matches `synthpop persons`."""
    import numpy as np

    from .persons import family_ids, locate

    persons = persons.assign(family_id=family_ids(persons, data["pums_persons"]))
    where = locate(persons, data["e911"], data["parcels"], np.random.default_rng([area.random_seed, 2]))
    cols = [v.id for v in catalog.active]
    seed = data["pums_persons"][["SERIALNO", "SPORDER", "AGEP", "POVPIP"]]
    p = (persons[["person_id", "family_id", "household_id", "parcel_id", "block", "seed_serial", "seed_person"] + cols]
         .merge(where, on="person_id")
         .merge(seed, left_on=["seed_serial", "seed_person"], right_on=["SERIALNO", "SPORDER"], how="left")
         .drop(columns=["SERIALNO", "SPORDER"])
         .rename(columns={"AGEP": "age", "POVPIP": "poverty_ratio"})
         .sort_values("person_id", ignore_index=True))
    p["u"] = np.random.default_rng([area.random_seed, 3]).random(len(p)).round(4)
    return p


RUN_KINDS = ("main", "draw", "replicate", "validation")


def run_names(runs_dir: str | Path) -> list[str]:
    """Saved runs in playback order: main, placement draws, replicates, validation."""
    runs = Path(runs_dir)
    names = ["main"] + sorted(d.name for d in runs.glob("draw_*")) + sorted(d.name for d in runs.glob("replicate_*")) + ["validation"]
    return [n for n in names if (runs / n / "persons.parquet").exists()]


def publish_people_runs(runs_dir: str | Path, data: dict, catalog, area: StudyArea, out_dir: str | Path) -> int:
    """people_runs/: every saved run's persons, for playing the simulations on the map.

    Only what differs between runs is stored per run, about 0.25 MB each:
      <run>.parquet   per person, in person_id order: seed (row in seeds), household_id,
                      in_family (family_id = household_id when true), point (row in points)
    and what is shared, once:
      seeds.parquet   one row per seed (PUMS) person any run uses: exact age and poverty
                      ratio and every catalog category, which depend only on the seed person
      points.parquet  every map point any run uses: lon, lat, parcel_id, block, location
      u.parquet       the fixed draw u by person_id; every run uses the same stream
      index.json      the runs in playback order, with kind, people and households
    """
    import numpy as np
    import pyarrow as pa
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq

    out = Path(out_dir) / "people_runs"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for old in out.glob("*.parquet"):
        old.unlink()
    key, where = ["seed_serial", "seed_person"], ["lon", "lat", "parcel_id"]
    attrs = ["age", "poverty_ratio"] + [v.id for v in catalog.active]
    frames = {name: people_frame(pd.read_parquet(Path(runs_dir) / name / "persons.parquet"), data, catalog, area)
              for name in run_names(runs_dir)}

    seeds = pd.concat([f[key + attrs] for f in frames.values()]).drop_duplicates(key, ignore_index=True)
    seeds.insert(0, "seed", np.arange(len(seeds), dtype="int16"))
    seeds.to_parquet(out / "seeds.parquet", index=False)
    points = pd.concat([f[where + ["block", "location"]] for f in frames.values()]).drop_duplicates(where, ignore_index=True)
    points.insert(0, "point", np.arange(len(points), dtype="int32"))
    points.to_parquet(out / "points.parquet", index=False, compression="zstd")
    longest = max(frames.values(), key=len)
    pd.DataFrame({"u": longest["u"].to_numpy()}).to_parquet(out / "u.parquet", index=False)

    index = []
    for name, f in frames.items():
        if not np.array_equal(f["u"].to_numpy(), longest["u"].to_numpy()[:len(f)]):
            raise ValueError(f"run {name} does not share the u stream")
        f = (f.merge(seeds[key + ["seed"]], on=key, how="left").merge(points[where + ["point"]], on=where, how="left")
             .sort_values("person_id", ignore_index=True))
        table = pa.table({"seed": f["seed"].astype("int16"), "household_id": f["household_id"].astype("int32"),
                          "in_family": f["family_id"].notna().to_numpy(), "point": f["point"].astype("int32")})
        pq.write_table(table, out / f"{name}.parquet", compression="zstd",
                       use_dictionary=["seed", "in_family", "point"], column_encoding={"household_id": "DELTA_BINARY_PACKED"})
        kind = next(k for k in RUN_KINDS if name.startswith(k))
        index.append({"name": name, "kind": kind, "people": len(f),
                      "households": int(f.loc[f["household_id"] >= 0, "household_id"].nunique())})
    (out / "index.json").write_text(json.dumps(index, indent=1) + "\n")
    return len(index)

    Everyone is counted, including people with a blank factor (education under 25).

    def people(self, run: str | None = None) -> bytes:
        """One run's synthetic persons as one columnar JSON document (the main run unless
        `run` names another). Each attribute is a list of codes into that variable's schema
        categories (-1 for blank), so the app can colour, filter and apply risk models with
        no more requests. The main run is built once; the last few other runs are cached."""
        if run in (None, "", "main"):
            if self._people is None:
                path = self.out / "people.parquet"
                if not path.exists():
                    raise KeyError("no people published; run `synthpop publish`")
                self._people = self._people_body(pd.read_parquet(path))
            return self._people
        if run not in {r["name"] for r in self.people_runs()}:
            raise KeyError(f"no run {run!r}")
        if run in self._run_cache:
            self._run_cache.move_to_end(run)
            return self._run_cache[run]
        body = self._people_body(self._run_frame(run))
        self._run_cache[run] = body
        while len(self._run_cache) > 8:
            self._run_cache.popitem(last=False)
        return body

    def _run_frame(self, run: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """A run's persons rebuilt from people_runs/: the run's own columns joined to the
        shared seed people, map points and u stream (see publish_people_runs)."""
        d = self.out / "people_runs"
        if self._shared is None:
            self._shared = (pd.read_parquet(d / "seeds.parquet").set_index("seed"),
                            pd.read_parquet(d / "points.parquet").set_index("point"),
                            pd.read_parquet(d / "u.parquet")["u"].to_numpy())
        seeds, points, u = self._shared
        f = pd.read_parquet(d / f"{run}.parquet")
        p = pd.concat([f[["household_id"]], seeds.loc[f["seed"]].reset_index(drop=True),
                       points.loc[f["point"]].reset_index(drop=True)], axis=1)
        p["family_id"] = p["household_id"].where(f["in_family"].to_numpy())
        p["u"] = u[:len(p)]
        return p

    def people_runs(self) -> list[dict]:
        """The runs the app can play, in order (main, placement draws, replicates,
        validation), each with its kind and how many people and households it has."""
        if self._runs is None:
            path = self.out / "people_runs" / "index.json"
            self._runs = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else [{"name": "main", "kind": "main"}]
        return self._runs

    def _people_body(self, p: pd.DataFrame) -> bytes:
        attrs = [v.id for v in self.catalog.active if v.id in p.columns]
        codes = {}
        for a in attrs:
            index = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(self.catalog.variable(a).category_ids)}
            codes[a] = p[a].astype(str).map(index).fillna(-1).astype(int).tolist()
        parcels, parcel_code = np.unique(p["parcel_id"].to_numpy(dtype=str), return_inverse=True)
        blocks, block_code = np.unique(p["block"].to_numpy(dtype=str), return_inverse=True)
        body = {
            "count": len(p), "lon": p["lon"].tolist(), "lat": p["lat"].tolist(),
            "age": p["age"].fillna(-1).astype(int).tolist(),
            # Income as % of the poverty line (-1 where poverty status is not determined).
            "poverty_ratio": p["poverty_ratio"].fillna(-1).astype(int).tolist() if "poverty_ratio" in p else [-1] * len(p),
            "u": p["u"].astype(float).round(4).tolist(),
            "household": p["household_id"].astype(int).tolist(),
            "family": p["family_id"].fillna(-1).astype(int).tolist() if "family_id" in p else [-1] * len(p),
            "parcel": parcel_code.tolist(), "parcels": parcels.tolist(),
            # Block ids start with their block group (12 digits) and tract (11), so one code covers every level.
            "block": block_code.tolist(), "blocks": blocks.tolist(),
            "fallback": (p["location"] == "parcel").astype(int).tolist(),
            "attributes": attrs, "codes": codes,
        }
        return json.dumps(body, separators=(",", ":")).encode()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ data points

    def people(self, run: str | None = None) -> bytes:
        """One run's synthetic persons as one columnar JSON document (the main run unless
        `run` names another). Each attribute is a list of codes into that variable's schema
        categories (-1 for blank), so the app can colour, filter and apply risk models with
        no more requests. The main run is built once; the last few other runs are cached."""
        if run in (None, "", "main"):
            if self._people is None:
                path = self.out / "people.parquet"
                if not path.exists():
                    raise KeyError("no people published; run `synthpop publish`")
                self._people = self._people_body(pd.read_parquet(path))
            return self._people
        if run not in {r["name"] for r in self.people_runs()}:
            raise KeyError(f"no run {run!r}")
        if run in self._run_cache:
            self._run_cache.move_to_end(run)
            return self._run_cache[run]
        body = self._people_body(self._run_frame(run))
        self._run_cache[run] = body
        while len(self._run_cache) > 8:
            self._run_cache.popitem(last=False)
        return body

    def _run_frame(self, run: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """A run's persons rebuilt from people_runs/: the run's own columns joined to the
        shared seed people, map points and u stream (see publish_people_runs)."""
        d = self.out / "people_runs"
        if self._shared is None:
            self._shared = (pd.read_parquet(d / "seeds.parquet").set_index("seed"),
                            pd.read_parquet(d / "points.parquet").set_index("point"),
                            pd.read_parquet(d / "u.parquet")["u"].to_numpy())
        seeds, points, u = self._shared
        f = pd.read_parquet(d / f"{run}.parquet")
        p = pd.concat([f[["household_id"]], seeds.loc[f["seed"]].reset_index(drop=True),
                       points.loc[f["point"]].reset_index(drop=True)], axis=1)
        p["family_id"] = p["household_id"].where(f["in_family"].to_numpy())
        p["u"] = u[:len(p)]
        return p

    def people_runs(self) -> list[dict]:
        """The runs the app can play, in order (main, placement draws, replicates,
        validation), each with its kind and how many people and households it has."""
        if self._runs is None:
            path = self.out / "people_runs" / "index.json"
            self._runs = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else [{"name": "main", "kind": "main"}]
        return self._runs

    def _people_body(self, p: pd.DataFrame) -> bytes:
        attrs = [v.id for v in self.catalog.active if v.id in p.columns]
        codes = {}
        for a in attrs:
            index = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(self.catalog.variable(a).category_ids)}
            codes[a] = p[a].astype(str).map(index).fillna(-1).astype(int).tolist()

        blocks, block_code = np.unique(p["block"].to_numpy(dtype=str), return_inverse=True)
        body = {

            "age": p["age"].fillna(-1).astype(int).tolist(),
            # Income as % of the poverty line (-1 where poverty status is not determined).
            "poverty_ratio": p["poverty_ratio"].fillna(-1).astype(int).tolist() if "poverty_ratio" in p else [-1] * len(p),
            "u": p["u"].astype(float).round(4).tolist(),
            "household": p["household_id"].astype(int).tolist(),
            "family": p["family_id"].fillna(-1).astype(int).tolist() if "family_id" in p else [-1] * len(p),
            "parcel": parcel_code.tolist(), "parcels": parcels.tolist(),
            # Block ids start with their block group (12 digits) and tract (11), so one code covers every level.
            "block": block_code.tolist(), "blocks": blocks.tolist(),
            "fallback": (p["location"] == "parcel").astype(int).tolist(),
            "attributes": attrs, "codes": codes,
        }
        return json.dumps(body, separators=(",", ":")).encode()

"""Household circles for the map: every household drawn as a circle on its parcel,
spread over the parcel instead of stacked on its E911 address point, with the circle's
area proportional to the number of people in it.

Layout happens in two steps:

- `slots` (at publish time) lays out, for every parcel and every number of units `n` it
  holds in any run, n points spread evenly over the parcel: a fine grid of candidate
  points inside the parcel, grouped into n clusters (k-means), each slot the candidate
  nearest its cluster's centre. Each slot gets `room`, the radius a circle there can
  have without reaching the parcel edge or the next slot's circle.
- `place` (per run, when the app asks for people) puts the parcel's units in those
  slots, the largest unit in the roomiest slot, and sizes them: radius R1·√size metres,
  shrunk by one factor per parcel when the largest would not fit.

A unit is a household, or all the group-quarters residents of one parcel (a dorm or
nursing home), who live in no household.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import shapely

R1 = 3.0                  # metres: radius of a one-person household's circle
CRS = 26919               # UTM 19N, metres
_ITER = 8                 # k-means iterations


def units(persons: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Each person's unit: their household, or -1 - (parcel row) for group quarters."""
    gq = persons["household_id"] < 0
    parcel_code = pd.factorize(persons["parcel_id"])[0]
    return pd.Series(np.where(gq, -1 - parcel_code, persons["household_id"]), index=persons.index)


def unit_counts(persons: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Number of units on each parcel (index parcel_id)."""
    u = pd.DataFrame({"parcel_id": persons["parcel_id"].to_numpy(), "unit": units(persons).to_numpy()})
    return u.drop_duplicates().groupby("parcel_id").size()


def slots(parcels, needs: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Slots for every (parcel_id, n) in `needs`: parcel_id, n, k, lon, lat, room (metres)."""
    import geopandas as gpd

    shapes = gpd.GeoSeries(parcels.set_index("parcel_id").geometry, crs=parcels.crs or 4326).to_crs(CRS)
    rows = []
    for pid, ns in needs.groupby("parcel_id")["n"]:
        if pid not in shapes.index:
            continue
        poly = shapes[pid]
        if poly is None or poly.is_empty:
            continue
        for n in sorted(set(ns)):
            xy, room = _layout(poly, int(n))
            rows.append(pd.DataFrame({"parcel_id": pid, "n": n, "k": np.arange(len(xy)), "x": xy[:, 0], "y": xy[:, 1], "room": room}))
    if not rows:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["parcel_id", "n", "k", "lon", "lat", "room"])
    out = pd.concat(rows, ignore_index=True)
    ll = gpd.GeoSeries(gpd.points_from_xy(out["x"], out["y"]), crs=CRS).to_crs(4326)
    out["lon"], out["lat"] = ll.x.round(7), ll.y.round(7)
    out["room"] = out["room"].round(2)
    return out[["parcel_id", "n", "k", "lon", "lat", "room"]].astype({"n": "int32", "k": "int32"})


def _layout(poly, n: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """n points spread evenly over a polygon (metres), and the room around each."""
    cand = _grid(poly, n)
    edge = shapely.distance(poly.boundary, shapely.points(cand))
    if n == 1:
        xy = cand[[int(np.argmax(edge))]]               # the point deepest inside
    else:
        # Farthest-point start from the deepest point, then k-means over the candidates.
        pick = [int(np.argmax(edge))]
        d = np.linalg.norm(cand - cand[pick[0]], axis=1)
        for _ in range(1, n):
            pick.append(int(np.argmax(d)))
            d = np.minimum(d, np.linalg.norm(cand - cand[pick[-1]], axis=1))
        centres = cand[pick].astype(float)
        for _ in range(_ITER):
            lab = np.argmin(((cand[:, None, :] - centres[None]) ** 2).sum(-1), axis=1)
            for k in range(n):
                m = lab == k
                if m.any():
                    centres[k] = cand[m].mean(axis=0)
        # Snap each centre to a distinct candidate inside the parcel.
        taken: set[int] = set()
        idx = []
        for c in centres:
            order = np.argsort(((cand - c) ** 2).sum(-1))
            j = next((int(o) for o in order if int(o) not in taken), int(order[0]))
            taken.add(j)
            idx.append(j)
        xy = cand[idx]
    edge_xy = shapely.distance(poly.boundary, shapely.points(xy))
    if len(xy) > 1:
        dist = np.linalg.norm(xy[:, None, :] - xy[None], axis=-1)
        np.fill_diagonal(dist, np.inf)
        room = np.minimum(edge_xy, dist.min(axis=1) / 2)
    else:
        room = edge_xy
    return xy, np.maximum(room, 0.3)


def _grid(poly, n: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """A hexagonal grid of points inside the polygon, about six per unit (at least n)."""
    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = poly.bounds
    g = max(0.3, float(np.sqrt(poly.area / (6 * n))))
    for _ in range(6):
        ys = np.arange(miny + g / 2, maxy, g * np.sqrt(3) / 2)
        xs = np.arange(minx + g / 2, maxx, g)
        X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
        X = X + (np.arange(len(ys)) % 2)[:, None] * g / 2
        x, y = X.ravel(), Y.ravel()
        ok = shapely.contains_xy(poly, x, y)
        if ok.sum() >= n:
            return np.column_stack([x[ok], y[ok]])
        g /= 2
    p = poly.representative_point()
    return np.array([[p.x, p.y]] * n)


def place(persons: pd.DataFrame, slot_table: pd.DataFrame | None) -> tuple[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Each person's unit index and the units: lon, lat, r (metres), size, parcel_id.

    Units are ordered by parcel, then size (largest first), then household id. A parcel
    without slots (no geometry, or a run with more units than any slot set) keeps its
    units on their members' address point."""
    key = units(persons).to_numpy()
    f = pd.DataFrame({"unit": key, "parcel_id": persons["parcel_id"].to_numpy(),
                      "lon": persons["lon"].to_numpy(), "lat": persons["lat"].to_numpy()})
    u = f.groupby("unit", sort=False).agg(parcel_id=("parcel_id", "first"), size=("lon", "size"),
                                          alon=("lon", "first"), alat=("lat", "first")).reset_index()
    u = u.sort_values(["parcel_id", "size", "unit"], ascending=[True, False, True], ignore_index=True)
    u["k"] = u.groupby("parcel_id").cumcount().astype("int32")
    u["n"] = u.groupby("parcel_id")["unit"].transform("size").astype("int32")
    if slot_table is not None and len(slot_table):
        # Roomiest slot first, so the largest unit gets it.
        s = slot_table.sort_values(["parcel_id", "n", "room"], ascending=[True, True, False]).copy()
        s["k"] = s.groupby(["parcel_id", "n"]).cumcount().astype("int32")
        u = u.merge(s[["parcel_id", "n", "k", "lon", "lat", "room"]], on=["parcel_id", "n", "k"], how="left")
    else:
        u[["lon", "lat", "room"]] = np.nan
    base = R1 * np.sqrt(u["size"].to_numpy())
    fit = (u["room"] / base).fillna(1.0)
    shrink = fit.groupby(u["parcel_id"]).transform("min").clip(upper=1.0)
    u["r"] = (base * shrink).round(2).clip(lower=0.3)
    u["lon"] = u["lon"].fillna(u["alon"])
    u["lat"] = u["lat"].fillna(u["alat"])
    index = pd.Series(np.arange(len(u)), index=u["unit"])
    return index.loc[key].to_numpy(), u[["lon", "lat", "r", "size", "parcel_id"]]

            pick.append(int(np.argmax(d)))
            d = np.minimum(d, np.linalg.norm(cand - cand[pick[-1]], axis=1))
        centres = cand[pick].astype(float)
        for _ in range(_ITER):
            lab = np.argmin(((cand[:, None, :] - centres[None]) ** 2).sum(-1), axis=1)
            for k in range(n):
                m = lab == k
                if m.any():
                    centres[k] = cand[m].mean(axis=0)
        # Snap each centre to a distinct candidate inside the parcel.
        taken: set[int] = set()
        idx = []
        for c in centres:
            order = np.argsort(((cand - c) ** 2).sum(-1))
            j = next((int(o) for o in order if int(o) not in taken), int(order[0]))
            taken.add(j)
            idx.append(j)
        xy = cand[idx]
    edge_xy = shapely.distance(poly.boundary, shapely.points(xy))
    if len(xy) > 1:
        dist = np.linalg.norm(xy[:, None, :] - xy[None], axis=-1)
        np.fill_diagonal(dist, np.inf)
        room = np.minimum(edge_xy, dist.min(axis=1) / 2)
    else:
        room = edge_xy
    return xy, np.maximum(room, 0.3)


def _grid(poly, n: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """A hexagonal grid of points inside the polygon, about six per unit (at least n)."""
    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = poly.bounds
    g = max(0.3, float(np.sqrt(poly.area / (6 * n))))
    for _ in range(6):
        ys = np.arange(miny + g / 2, maxy, g * np.sqrt(3) / 2)
        xs = np.arange(minx + g / 2, maxx, g)
        X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
        X = X + (np.arange(len(ys)) % 2)[:, None] * g / 2
        x, y = X.ravel(), Y.ravel()
        ok = shapely.contains_xy(poly, x, y)
        if ok.sum() >= n:
            return np.column_stack([x[ok], y[ok]])
        g /= 2
    p = poly.representative_point()
    return np.array([[p.x, p.y]] * n)


def place(persons: pd.DataFrame, slot_table: pd.DataFrame | None) -> tuple[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Each person's unit index and the units: lon, lat, r (metres), size, parcel_id.

    Units are ordered by parcel, then size (largest first), then household id. A parcel
    without slots (no geometry, or a run with more units than any slot set) keeps its
    units on their members' address point."""
    key = units(persons).to_numpy()
    f = pd.DataFrame({"unit": key, "parcel_id": persons["parcel_id"].to_numpy(),
                      "lon": persons["lon"].to_numpy(), "lat": persons["lat"].to_numpy()})
    u = f.groupby("unit", sort=False).agg(parcel_id=("parcel_id", "first"), size=("lon", "size"),
                                          alon=("lon", "first"), alat=("lat", "first")).reset_index()
    u = u.sort_values(["parcel_id", "size", "unit"], ascending=[True, False, True], ignore_index=True)
    u["k"] = u.groupby("parcel_id").cumcount().astype("int32")
    u["n"] = u.groupby("parcel_id")["unit"].transform("size").astype("int32")
    if slot_table is not None and len(slot_table):
        # Roomiest slot first, so the largest unit gets it.
        s = slot_table.sort_values(["parcel_id", "n", "room"], ascending=[True, True, False]).copy()
        s["k"] = s.groupby(["parcel_id", "n"]).cumcount().astype("int32")
        u = u.merge(s[["parcel_id", "n", "k", "lon", "lat", "room"]], on=["parcel_id", "n", "k"], how="left")
    else:
        u[["lon", "lat", "room"]] = np.nan
    base = R1 * np.sqrt(u["size"].to_numpy())
    fit = (u["room"] / base).fillna(1.0)
    shrink = fit.groupby(u["parcel_id"]).transform("min").clip(upper=1.0)
    u["r"] = (base * shrink).round(2).clip(lower=0.3)
    u["lon"] = u["lon"].fillna(u["alon"])
    u["lat"] = u["lat"].fillna(u["alat"])
    index = pd.Series(np.arange(len(u)), index=u["unit"])
    return index.loc[key].to_numpy(), u[["lon", "lat", "r", "size", "parcel_id"]]

"""Household circles for the map: every household drawn as a circle on its parcel,
spread over the parcel instead of stacked on its E911 address point, with the circle's
area proportional to the number of people in it.

Layout happens in two steps:

- `slots` (at publish time) lays out, for every parcel and every number of units `n` it
  holds in any run, n points spread evenly over the parcel: a fine grid of candidate
  points inside the parcel, grouped into n clusters (k-means), each slot the candidate
  nearest its cluster's centre. Each slot gets `room`, the radius a circle there can
  have without reaching the parcel edge or the next slot's circle.
- `place` (per run, when the app asks for people) puts the parcel's units in those
  slots, the largest unit in the roomiest slot, and sizes them: radius R1·√size metres,
  shrunk by one factor per parcel when the largest would not fit.

A unit is a household, or all the group-quarters residents of one parcel (a dorm or
nursing home), who live in no household.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import shapely

R1 = 3.0                  # metres: radius of a one-person household's circle
CRS = 26919               # UTM 19N, metres
_ITER = 8                 # k-means iterations


def units(persons: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Each person's unit: their household, or -1 - (parcel row) for group quarters."""
    gq = persons["household_id"] < 0
    parcel_code = pd.factorize(persons["parcel_id"])[0]
    return pd.Series(np.where(gq, -1 - parcel_code, persons["household_id"]), index=persons.index)


def unit_counts(persons: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Number of units on each parcel (index parcel_id)."""
    u = pd.DataFrame({"parcel_id": persons["parcel_id"].to_numpy(), "unit": units(persons).to_numpy()})
    return u.drop_duplicates().groupby("parcel_id").size()


def slots(parcels, needs: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Slots for every (parcel_id, n) in `needs`: parcel_id, n, k, lon, lat, room (metres)."""
    import geopandas as gpd

    shapes = gpd.GeoSeries(parcels.set_index("parcel_id").geometry, crs=parcels.crs or 4326).to_crs(CRS)
    rows = []
    for pid, ns in needs.groupby("parcel_id")["n"]:
        if pid not in shapes.index:
            continue
        poly = shapes[pid]
        if poly is None or poly.is_empty:
            continue
        for n in sorted(set(ns)):
            xy, room = _layout(poly, int(n))
            rows.append(pd.DataFrame({"parcel_id": pid, "n": n, "k": np.arange(len(xy)), "x": xy[:, 0], "y": xy[:, 1], "room": room}))
    if not rows:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["parcel_id", "n", "k", "lon", "lat", "room"])
    out = pd.concat(rows, ignore_index=True)
    ll = gpd.GeoSeries(gpd.points_from_xy(out["x"], out["y"]), crs=CRS).to_crs(4326)
    out["lon"], out["lat"] = ll.x.round(7), ll.y.round(7)
    out["room"] = out["room"].round(2)
    return out[["parcel_id", "n", "k", "lon", "lat", "room"]].astype({"n": "int32", "k": "int32"})


def _layout(poly, n: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """n points spread evenly over a polygon (metres), and the room around each."""
    cand = _grid(poly, n)
    edge = shapely.distance(poly.boundary, shapely.points(cand))
    if n == 1:
        xy = cand[[int(np.argmax(edge))]]               # the point deepest inside
    else:
        # Farthest-point start from the deepest point, then k-means over the candidates.
        pick = [int(np.argmax(edge))]
        d = np.linalg.norm(cand - cand[pick[0]], axis=1)
        for _ in range(1, n):
            pick.append(int(np.argmax(d)))
            d = np.minimum(d, np.linalg.norm(cand - cand[pick[-1]], axis=1))
        centres = cand[pick].astype(float)
        for _ in range(_ITER):
            lab = np.argmin(((cand[:, None, :] - centres[None]) ** 2).sum(-1), axis=1)
            for k in range(n):
                m = lab == k
                if m.any():
                    centres[k] = cand[m].mean(axis=0)
        # Snap each centre to a distinct candidate inside the parcel.
        taken: set[int] = set()
        idx = []
        for c in centres:
            order = np.argsort(((cand - c) ** 2).sum(-1))
            j = next((int(o) for o in order if int(o) not in taken), int(order[0]))
            taken.add(j)
            idx.append(j)
        xy = cand[idx]
    edge_xy = shapely.distance(poly.boundary, shapely.points(xy))
    if len(xy) > 1:
        dist = np.linalg.norm(xy[:, None, :] - xy[None], axis=-1)
        np.fill_diagonal(dist, np.inf)
        room = np.minimum(edge_xy, dist.min(axis=1) / 2)
    else:
        room = edge_xy
    return xy, np.maximum(room, 0.3)


def _grid(poly, n: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """A hexagonal grid of points inside the polygon, about six per unit (at least n)."""
    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = poly.bounds
    g = max(0.3, float(np.sqrt(poly.area / (6 * n))))
    for _ in range(6):
        ys = np.arange(miny + g / 2, maxy, g * np.sqrt(3) / 2)
        xs = np.arange(minx + g / 2, maxx, g)
        X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
        X = X + (np.arange(len(ys)) % 2)[:, None] * g / 2
        x, y = X.ravel(), Y.ravel()
        ok = shapely.contains_xy(poly, x, y)
        if ok.sum() >= n:
            return np.column_stack([x[ok], y[ok]])
        g /= 2
    p = poly.representative_point()
    return np.array([[p.x, p.y]] * n)


def place(persons: pd.DataFrame, slot_table: pd.DataFrame | None) -> tuple[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Each person's unit index and the units: lon, lat, r (metres), size, parcel_id.

    Units are ordered by parcel, then size (largest first), then household id. A parcel
    without slots (no geometry, or a run with more units than any slot set) keeps its
    units on their members' address point."""
    key = units(persons).to_numpy()
    f = pd.DataFrame({"unit": key, "parcel_id": persons["parcel_id"].to_numpy(),
                      "lon": persons["lon"].to_numpy(), "lat": persons["lat"].to_numpy()})
    u = f.groupby("unit", sort=False).agg(parcel_id=("parcel_id", "first"), size=("lon", "size"),
                                          alon=("lon", "first"), alat=("lat", "first")).reset_index()
    u = u.sort_values(["parcel_id", "size", "unit"], ascending=[True, False, True], ignore_index=True)
    u["k"] = u.groupby("parcel_id").cumcount().astype("int32")
    u["n"] = u.groupby("parcel_id")["unit"].transform("size").astype("int32")
    if slot_table is not None and len(slot_table):
        # Roomiest slot first, so the largest unit gets it.
        s = slot_table.sort_values(["parcel_id", "n", "room"], ascending=[True, True, False]).copy()
        s["k"] = s.groupby(["parcel_id", "n"]).cumcount().astype("int32")
        u = u.merge(s[["parcel_id", "n", "k", "lon", "lat", "room"]], on=["parcel_id", "n", "k"], how="left")
    else:
        u[["lon", "lat", "room"]] = np.nan
    base = R1 * np.sqrt(u["size"].to_numpy())
    fit = (u["room"] / base).fillna(1.0)
    shrink = fit.groupby(u["parcel_id"]).transform("min").clip(upper=1.0)
    u["r"] = (base * shrink).round(2).clip(lower=0.3)
    u["lon"] = u["lon"].fillna(u["alon"])
    u["lat"] = u["lat"].fillna(u["alat"])
    index = pd.Series(np.arange(len(u)), index=u["unit"])
    return index.loc[key].to_numpy(), u[["lon", "lat", "r", "size", "parcel_id"]]

lines: -// The people layer: every synthetic person of the main run as a dot on their E911
-// address point, stacked upward where several share one (apartment buildings). By default
-// each address point splits into side-by-side columns, one per colour group (e.g. one per
-// age band), so a building reads as a small bar chart of who lives there.
+// The people layer: every synthetic household of one run as a circle on its parcel. The
+// circles are spread over the parcel rather than stacked on the E911 address point, and a
+// circle's area is proportional to the number of people in it (the layout comes from the
+// server: synthpop/households.py). A parcel's group-quarters residents (dorm, nursing
+// home) form one circle. Clicking a household selects it: its people appear inside the
+// circle as dots, and each person can be clicked in turn.
// Everything after the one download runs in the browser, so colouring, filtering and
// data points react instantly. A data point marks a person a case when their fixed
// draw u is below their risk, so moving a slider adds or removes cases at the margin
-export const MIN_ZOOM = 14;          // people show from block zoom down
-const FLOOR_M = 2.5;                 // height between people stacked on one address point
-const COLUMN_GAP_PX = 2;             // space between side-by-side columns, beyond one dot
+export const MIN_ZOOM = 14;          // households show from block zoom down
export type PeopleFilter = { by: string; values: string[] };
export type Focus = { level: string; id: string };
-// focus: the area open in the detail panel; people outside it are faded.
-// stack: "split" puts each colour group in its own column at an address point; "single"

def test_people_are_one_columnar_document_coded_by_schema_category(atlas, catalog):
    body = json.loads(atlas.people())
    n = body["count"]
    assert n > 0 and all(len(body[k]) == n for k in ("lon", "lat", "age", "u", "household", "family", "poverty_ratio", "parcel", "block", "fallback"))
    assert all(0 <= u < 1 for u in body["u"])
    for a in body["attributes"]:
        cats = catalog.variable(a).category_ids
        assert len(body["codes"][a]) == n and all(-1 <= c < len(cats) for c in body["codes"][a])
    sex = catalog.variable("sex").category_ids
    p = pd.read_parquet(atlas.out / "people.parquet")
    assert [sex[c] for c in body["codes"]["sex"]] == p["sex"].astype(str).tolist()
    assert {body["parcels"][i] for i in body["parcel"]} <= set(p["parcel_id"])
    assert [body["blocks"][i] for i in body["block"]] == p["block"].tolist()
    assert sum(body["fallback"]) == int((p["location"] == "parcel").sum())

import geopandas as gpd
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import shapely

from synthpop.households import CRS, R1, place, slots, unit_counts


def _parcels():
    """Two parcels in metres (UTM 19N) near Portland: a 40 m square and a 60 x 20 m strip."""
    x0, y0 = 398000, 4835000
    g = gpd.GeoDataFrame({"parcel_id": ["A", "B"]}, geometry=[shapely.box(x0, y0, x0 + 40, y0 + 40),
                                                              shapely.box(x0 + 100, y0, x0 + 160, y0 + 20)], crs=CRS)
    return g.to_crs(4326)


def _persons():
    # Parcel A: households 1 (3 people), 2 (1), 3 (2) and two group-quarters residents.
    # Parcel B: household 4 (5 people).
    hh = [1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3, -1, -1, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4]
    parcel = ["A"] * 8 + ["B"] * 5
    return pd.DataFrame({"person_id": range(len(hh)), "household_id": hh, "parcel_id": parcel,
                         "lon": -70.26, "lat": 43.66})


def test_slots_spread_units_evenly_inside_their_parcel():
    parcels = _parcels()
    table = slots(parcels, pd.DataFrame({"parcel_id": ["A", "A", "B"], "n": [1, 4, 2]}))
    assert sorted(table.groupby(["parcel_id", "n"]).size().items()) == [(("A", 1), 1), (("A", 4), 4), (("B", 2), 2)]
    shapes = parcels.set_index("parcel_id").to_crs(CRS).geometry
    pts = gpd.GeoSeries(gpd.points_from_xy(table["lon"], table["lat"]), crs=4326).to_crs(CRS)
    assert all(shapes[p].contains(pt) for p, pt in zip(table["parcel_id"], pts))
    one = pts[(table["parcel_id"] == "A").to_numpy() & (table["n"] == 1).to_numpy()].iloc[0]
    assert one.distance(shapes["A"].centroid) < 3                  # a lone household sits mid-parcel
    four = np.array([[p.x, p.y] for p in pts[((table["parcel_id"] == "A") & (table["n"] == 4)).to_numpy()]])
    d = np.linalg.norm(four[:, None] - four[None], axis=-1)[np.triu_indices(4, 1)]
    assert d.min() > 12                                           # four slots on a 40 m square, well apart
    assert (table["room"] > 0).all()

    persons = _persons()
    assert unit_counts(persons).to_dict() == {"A": 4, "B": 1}

    unit, u = place(persons, table)

    assert u["size"].tolist() == [3, 2, 2, 1, 5]                  # parcel A largest first, then parcel B
    # area proportional to size within a parcel, and no larger than R1·√size
    a = u[u["parcel_id"] == "A"]
    assert np.allclose(a["r"] / np.sqrt(a["size"]), a["r"].iloc[0] / np.sqrt(3), atol=0.02)
    assert (u["r"] <= R1 * np.sqrt(u["size"]) + 1e-9).all()
    # circles on one parcel never overlap
    xy = gpd.GeoSeries(gpd.points_from_xy(a["lon"], a["lat"]), crs=4326).to_crs(CRS)
    xy = np.array([[p.x, p.y] for p in xy])
    r = a["r"].to_numpy()
    for i in range(len(a)):

    persons = _persons()
    unit, u = place(persons, None)
    assert np.allclose(u["lon"], -70.26) and np.allclose(u["r"], R1 * np.sqrt(u["size"]))

lines: The main run gives 68,754 persons in 33,338 households and 14,748 families; 99.6% sit on an E911 address point.

-In the app, **People → Person table (one run)** opens the same table over the bottom of the map: all 68,754 rows, 100 a page, following the sidebar's people filters. Search finds a person, family or household by number, or a parcel by ID. **Download CSV** saves the matching rows, and clicking a row flies to that person and opens their parcel.

+In the app, **People → Person table (one run)** opens the same table over the bottom of the map: all 68,754 rows, 100 a page, following the sidebar's people filters. Search finds a person, family or household by number, or a parcel by ID. **Download CSV** saves the matching rows, and clicking a row flies to that person's household and opens it with them picked.

- **Data points apply automatically.** Every saved data point, and the one open in the editor, gives each person a case (1) or not (0): a person is a case when `u` is below their risk from the model. Because `u` is fixed, moving a slider only adds or removes cases at the margin; it never reshuffles who has the condition. People outside the model's universe (under 65 for dementia) are shown faint.
- **Colour people by** any data point or attribute. People open coloured by the first saved data point.
- **Show only people where** stacks filters on data points (case / not a case) or attributes. The legend counts the people shown.

-- People appear from block zoom (14) down. People sharing an address point stack upward 2.5 m apart, so apartment buildings read as columns. **Stack people at an address** sets how: *One column per colour* (the default) gives each colour group its own column side by side, in legend order from west to east (with Age, one column each for under 18, 18–34, 35–64 and 65+), so a building reads as a small bar chart; *One column, sorted by colour* keeps one column with the groups in bands. Only people passing the filters stack, so filtering leaves no gaps, and columns are spaced in screen pixels so they touch without overlapping at any zoom. While people are shown, 3D buildings (parcels, blocks) turn see-through, so the people columns inside and behind them stay visible. The **3D** button under the map's zoom controls, or **3D buildings and areas** in the sidebar, turns extrusion on or off; with it off, areas lie flat and faint under the people.

+- **Households, not dots.** From block zoom (14) down, every household is a circle on its parcel, and all the group-quarters residents of one parcel (a dorm, nursing home or shelter) form one more. Circles are spread over the parcel rather than stacked on the address point, and a circle's area is proportional to the people in it (see *Household circles* below).

+- **Colour.** A household takes its householder's colour (the Census convention: households by age, race or tenure of householder), or its first member's for group quarters. Coloured by a data point, a household is a case when anyone in it is. The legend still counts people. With filters on, a household shows when anyone in it passes, and takes its colour from the people who pass.

Click a person, on the map or in the card, to see everything about them. **Open parcel** opens the parcel's detail panel; × or Esc closes the household.

+- While households are shown, 3D buildings (parcels, blocks) turn see-through, so the circles under them stay visible. The **3D** button under the map's zoom controls, or **3D buildings and areas** in the sidebar, turns extrusion on or off; with it off, areas lie flat and faint under the households.
- While a saved data point is being edited, filters on it follow the draft; closing without saving puts them back.

-- **Clicking an area** (tract, block group, block or parcel) adds "Synthetic people here" to its detail panel: people, households, median age, share female, group-quarters residents and cases for each data point, counted from the dots. People outside the area fade. Clicking while zoomed out flies in to the area's people; "Show on map" does the same later. Clicking a dot opens its parcel.

+- **Clicking an area** (tract, block group, block or parcel) adds "Synthetic people here" to its detail panel: people, households, median age, share female, group-quarters residents and cases for each data point, counted from the people. Households outside the area fade. Clicking while zoomed out flies in to the area's households; "Show on map" does the same later.

- **People table** toggles a table of the area's people with the same columns as the CSV (plus block and one column per data point: 1 case, 0 not, blank outside the universe). It shows up to 500 rows; **Download CSV** gives all of them.

- Closing the player goes back to the main run.

Each is also *calibrated*: a variable with a block-group constraint in `config/variables.yaml`, so the fit matches each block group's published ACS counts within their margins. +`synthpop publish` also writes `data/out/people.parquet`: the same main-run persons and points, plus each person's catalog categories, exact poverty ratio and a fixed uniform draw `u`. `/api/people` serves them as one columnar JSON document (about 1.2 MB gzipped). After that single download the app does everything in the browser:

- **Data points apply automatically.** Every saved data point, and the one open in the editor, gives each person a case (1) or not (0): a person is a case when `u` is below their risk from the model. Because `u` is fixed, moving a slider only adds or removes cases at the margin; it never reshuffles who has the condition. People outside the model's universe (under 65 for dementia) are shown faint.
- **Colour people by** any data point or attribute. People open coloured by the first saved data point.
- While the player is open, households show at every zoom, so the whole city can be watched. Household ids differ between runs, so an open household closes when the run changes.
- Colours, filters, data points, the legend and the person table all follow the run on screen. Data points are reapplied to each run's people, so case counts change from run to run.
-- Runs load on demand (about 0.85 MB gzipped each), three ahead of the playhead; the server keeps the last eight.
+- Runs load on demand (about 1.2 MB gzipped each), three ahead of the playhead; the server keeps the last eight.
- Closing the player goes back to the main run.

`synthpop publish` writes the runs to `data/out/people_runs/` (about 25 MB for all 102). A person's attributes depend only on the seed person they copy, so they are stored once (`seeds.parquet`), as are the map points (`points.parquet`) and `u` (`u.parquet`, one stream shared by every run). Each `<run>.parquet` keeps only seed, household, a family flag and point, about 0.25 MB. `/api/people/runs` lists the runs and `/api/people?run=<name>` serves any of them in the same form as the main run.

Clicking one shows its people, and you can click each person. All 46 tests pass, and I tried it in the local app at http://localhost:8000/map/.

**What you'll see**
- **Circles:** from block zoom in, each household is a circle on its parcel. A circle's area is proportional to how many people live in it, about 3 m across per person's share. A parcel's dorm or nursing-home residents form one circle of their own.
- **Spread:** circles are evenly spaced over the parcel, so apartment parcels show many circles side by side. On a crowded parcel every circle shrinks by the same amount, so they never overlap and sizes stay comparable.
- **Colour:** a household takes its householder's colour, which is how the Census reports households by age, race or tenure. With a data point it shows as a case if anyone in it is. The legend still counts people.
- **Click a household:** the map zooms in until the circle is big, and its people appear inside as dots, householder at the top. A card lists them with their role (householder, relative, not related), age and sex, plus the household's tenure and family.
- **Click a person,** on the map or in the card, to see everything about them. **Open parcel** opens the parcel's details. × or Esc closes the household.
- **Person table:** clicking a row now goes to that person's household and opens it with them picked.
- **Simulation player:** it works with households too. Changing run closes the open household, because household IDs differ between runs.

**How the circles are placed**
- **When:** `synthpop publish` works out the circle positions for every parcel. That adds about a minute and writes `data/out/household_slots.parquet` (3.4 MB).
- **How:** it spreads points evenly over the parcel's outline, and a lone house sits in the middle of its lot.
- **Code:** the layout is in [synthpop/households.py](synthpop/households.py), with new tests in [tests/test_households.py](tests/test_households.py).

**Trade-offs**
- **No columns:** the "Stack people at an address" option and the per-age columns are gone, replaced by circles.
- **Position inside a parcel means nothing:** the model places households on parcels, not on units in a building.
- **Table and CSV:** `lon`/`lat` there are still each person's E911 address point. The circle position is only where the map draws the household.
- **Download size:** each run's download grew from about 0.85 MB to 1.2 MB gzipped, and `data/out` is now about 78 MB. I updated the README, the AWS deploy doc and [docs/person-table.md](docs/person-table.md).

# Codebase Design

Design **deep modules**: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface, placed at a clean seam, testable through that interface. Use this language and these principles wherever code is being designed or restructured. The aim is leverage for callers, locality for maintainers, and testability for everyone.

## Glossary

Use these terms exactly: don't substitute "component," "service," "API," or "boundary." Consistent language is the whole point.

**Module**: anything with an interface and an implementation. Deliberately scale-agnostic: a function, class, package, or tier-spanning slice. _Avoid_: unit, component, service.

**Interface**: everything a caller must know to use the module correctly: the type signature, but also invariants, ordering constraints, error modes, required configuration, and performance characteristics. _Avoid_: API, signature (too narrow, they refer only to the type-level surface).

**Implementation**: what's inside a module, its body of code. Distinct from **Adapter**: a thing can be a small adapter with a large implementation (a Postgres repo) or a large adapter with a small implementation (an in-memory fake). Reach for "adapter" when the seam is the topic; "implementation" otherwise.

**Depth**: leverage at the interface. The amount of behaviour a caller (or test) can exercise per unit of interface they have to learn. A module is **deep** when a large amount of behaviour sits behind a small interface, **shallow** when the interface is nearly as complex as the implementation.

**Seam** _(Michael Feathers)_: a place where you can alter behaviour without editing in that place; the *location* at which a module's interface lives. Where to put the seam is its own design decision, distinct from what goes behind it. _Avoid_: boundary (overloaded with DDD's bounded context).

**Adapter**: a concrete thing that satisfies an interface at a seam. Describes *role* (what slot it fills), not substance (what's inside).

**Leverage**: what callers get from depth. More capability per unit of interface they learn. One implementation pays back across N call sites and M tests.

**Locality**: what maintainers get from depth. Change, bugs, knowledge, and verification concentrate in one place rather than spreading across callers. Fix once, fixed everywhere.

## Deep vs shallow

**Deep module** = small interface + lots of implementation:

```
┌─────────────────────┐
│   Small Interface   │  ← Few methods, simple params
├─────────────────────┤
│                     │
│  Deep Implementation│  ← Complex logic hidden
│                     │
└─────────────────────┘
```

**Shallow module** = large interface + little implementation (avoid):

```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│       Large Interface           │  ← Many methods, complex params
├─────────────────────────────────┤
│  Thin Implementation            │  ← Just passes through
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```

When designing an interface, ask:

- Can I reduce the number of methods?
- Can I simplify the parameters?
- Can I hide more complexity inside?

## Principles

- **Depth is a property of the interface, not the implementation.** A deep module can be internally composed of small, mockable, swappable parts; they just aren't part of the interface. A module can have **internal seams** (private to its implementation, used by its own tests) as well as the **external seam** at its interface.
- **The deletion test.** Imagine deleting the module. If complexity vanishes, it was a pass-through. If complexity reappears across N callers, it was earning its keep.
- **The interface is the test surface.** Callers and tests cross the same seam. If you want to test *past* the interface, the module is probably the wrong shape.
- **One adapter means a hypothetical seam. Two adapters means a real one.** Don't introduce a seam unless something actually varies across it.

## Designing for testability

Good interfaces make testing natural:

1. **Accept dependencies, don't create them.**

   ```typescript
   // Testable
   function processOrder(order, paymentGateway) {}

   // Hard to test
   function processOrder(order) {
     const gateway = new StripeGateway();
   }
   ```

2. **Return results, don't produce side effects.**

   ```typescript
   // Testable
   function calculateDiscount(cart): Discount {}

   // Hard to test
   function applyDiscount(cart): void {
     cart.total -= discount;
   }
   ```

3. **Small surface area.** Fewer methods = fewer tests needed. Fewer params = simpler test setup.

## Relationships

- A **Module** has exactly one **Interface** (the surface it presents to callers and tests).
- **Depth** is a property of a **Module**, measured against its **Interface**.
- A **Seam** is where a **Module**'s **Interface** lives.
- An **Adapter** sits at a **Seam** and satisfies the **Interface**.
- **Depth** produces **Leverage** for callers and **Locality** for maintainers.

## Rejected framings

- **Depth as ratio of implementation-lines to interface-lines** (Ousterhout): rewards padding the implementation. We use depth-as-leverage instead.
- **"Interface" as the TypeScript `interface` keyword or a class's public methods**: too narrow: interface here includes every fact a caller must know.
- **"Boundary"**: overloaded with DDD's bounded context. Say **seam** or **interface**.

## Going deeper

- **Deepening a cluster given its dependencies**, see [DEEPENING.md](DEEPENING.md): dependency categories, seam discipline, and replace-don't-layer testing.
- **Exploring alternative interfaces**, see [DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md](DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md): spin up parallel sub-agents to design the interface several radically different ways, then compare on depth, locality, and seam placement.

# Deepening

How to deepen a cluster of shallow modules safely, given its dependencies. Assumes the vocabulary in [SKILL.md](SKILL.md): **module**, **interface**, **seam**, **adapter**.

## Dependency categories

When assessing a candidate for deepening, classify its dependencies. The category determines how the deepened module is tested across its seam.

### 1. In-process

Pure computation, in-memory state, no I/O. Always deepenable: merge the modules and test through the new interface directly. No adapter needed.

### 2. Local-substitutable

Dependencies that have local test stand-ins (PGLite for Postgres, in-memory filesystem). Deepenable if the stand-in exists. The deepened module is tested with the stand-in running in the test suite. The seam is internal; no port at the module's external interface.

### 3. Remote but owned (Ports & Adapters)

Your own services across a network boundary (microservices, internal APIs). Define a **port** (interface) at the seam. The deep module owns the logic; the transport is injected as an **adapter**. Tests use an in-memory adapter. Production uses an HTTP/gRPC/queue adapter.

Recommendation shape: *"Define a port at the seam, implement an HTTP adapter for production and an in-memory adapter for testing, so the logic sits in one deep module even though it's deployed across a network."*

### 4. True external (Mock)

Third-party services (Stripe, Twilio, etc.) you don't control. The deepened module takes the external dependency as an injected port; tests provide a mock adapter.

## Seam discipline

- **One adapter means a hypothetical seam. Two adapters means a real one.** Don't introduce a port unless at least two adapters are justified (typically production + test). A single-adapter seam is just indirection.
- **Internal seams vs external seams.** A deep module can have internal seams (private to its implementation, used by its own tests) as well as the external seam at its interface. Don't expose internal seams through the interface just because tests use them.

## Testing strategy: replace, don't layer

- Old unit tests on shallow modules become waste once tests at the deepened module's interface exist; delete them.
- Write new tests at the deepened module's interface. The **interface is the test surface**.
- Tests assert on observable outcomes through the interface, not internal state.
- Tests should survive internal refactors, since they describe behaviour, not implementation. If a test has to change when the implementation changes, it's testing past the interface.

content.text:
`/mattpocock-skills:improve-codebase-architecture` isn't installed here, so I used the nearest skill, `mattpocock-skills:codebase-design`. The ideas are in two groups: ways to restructure the code, then ways to improve the map. I haven't changed any code.

## Code structure, most valuable first

The skill rates a module by its **depth**: how much behaviour sits behind how small an interface. A shallow module makes every caller learn nearly as much as it hides.

**1. Split `PeopleLayer`, the class behind the people layer.** [people.ts](app/src/people.ts) is 521 lines and does six jobs:
- reading the run's data;
- working out data-point cases;
- filtering and colouring;
- the open household;
- the map layers;
- the HTML for tooltips, legend, table, CSV and summary.

It exposes about 20 members, and `main.ts`, the household card and the person table each use a different subset. Every new attribute touches several of them. I'd split it three ways:
- **Population:** one run's people behind `person(i)`, `household(u)`, `members(u)`, `role(i)` and `dims()`. It hides the encodings: −1 for blanks, parcel codes, unit indexes, householder first. It's pure code, so it can get the app's first front-end tests.
- **PeopleView:** the filters, colour and open household, plus the counts and visible households worked out from them. Caching lives in this one place instead of in keys built from `JSON.stringify` and three scattered `view = null` resets.
- **Renderers:** the map layers, legend, card and table each just read the view.

**2. Stop editing the open household from outside.** `main.ts` assigns `people.selection` in five places, and the card reads it directly. It should go through PeopleView: `open(u, person?)`, `pick(i)`, `close()`, with one change event. This is cheap to do as part of #1.

**3. The case rule is written twice.** `outcomes()` in people.ts repeats the logit and universe rule from [datapoints.py](synthpop/datapoints.py). If one changes without the other, the case counts on the map quietly stop matching the area estimates. I'd keep both, because moving it to the server would make the sliders laggy. A shared file of sample cases, checked by a test on each side, would keep them in step.

**4. One way to get a run's people.** The main run is stored twice: in `people.parquet` and in the `people_runs/` files. There's a test whose only job is to prove the two copies match. Removing `publish_people` and serving main like every other run would remove the special case in `atlas.people()` and save 2 MB. A small `RunPeople` module (`names()`, `frame(run)`, `document(run)`) would keep the storage layout private.

**5. Household layout logic lives in three places:**
- placing circles on parcels at publish time;
- sizing them on each request, in the atlas;
- drawing them in TypeScript: member layout, metres-to-degrees and the zoom-to-fit numbers in `main.ts`.

The constants are split across Python and TypeScript too. Lower priority: have `households.py` own its own file, and move the zoom-to-fit maths into PeopleView.

## Map and product ideas

- **Put households inside building footprints, not anywhere on the parcel.** Right now circles can land on lawns and parking lots. Building outlines from Maine's GeoLibrary or Microsoft's footprints would put apartment households inside the building, and in 3D they could stack by floor. Of all these ideas, this is the biggest gain in realism.
- **Household-level filters and colours:** size, family type (married couple, single parent, living alone), tenure, has a child, has someone 65+, anyone a case. Filters today only work on people.
- **Mixed households:** a segmented ring of member colours, so a grandparent living with children shows both.
- **Compare runs:** in the player, highlight which households on a parcel change between runs, to show how stable placement is.
- **Shareable links:** put the map position and open household in the URL, and let the search box find households by ID.
- **Smaller downloads:** a binary column format such as Arrow instead of JSON would roughly halve the 1.2 MB per run.

I'd start with #1 and #2. They're pure code that can be tested in isolation, and almost every map idea above would otherwise grow `PeopleLayer` further.

content.text:
`PeopleLayer` is now split into four parts, and the app's front end has tests for the first time: 20, all passing. In the local app, the household circles, card, person table, Esc and the simulation player all work as before, with no console errors.

## The new parts

| File | What it does | What callers use |
|---|---|---|
| [population.ts](app/src/population.ts) | One run's people with data points applied. It's now the only code that reads the raw download (−1 blanks, parcel codes, householder flag, circles). | `person(i)`, `household(u)`, `members(u)`, `dims()`, `label()`, `idSearch()`, `inArea()`, `csv()`, `summary()`, `setRun()`, `setDraft()` |
| [peopleView.ts](app/src/peopleView.ts) | The sidebar choices, the open household, and everything worked out from them: who's visible, colours, counts. | `derived()`, `colour(i)`, `open()`, `pick()`, `close()`, `setRun()`, `onChange` |
| [peopleLayers.ts](app/src/peopleLayers.ts) | The household and member layers on the map, plus their tooltips. | `peopleLayers(view, zoom)`, `peopleTooltip(view, info)` |
| [peoplePanels.ts](app/src/peoplePanels.ts) | Tooltips, legend, the sidebar's People section and the "Synthetic people here" panel. | Rendering functions only |

The household card and person table now read only from `PeopleView`, and `people.ts` is deleted.

## What got simpler
- **The open household:** `main.ts` used to change it directly in five places. Now it goes through `open`, `pick` and `close`, and one `onChange` redraws the map and zooms to the household.
- **Refreshing:** three scattered "throw away and rebuild" calls became one rule. Population keeps a version number that goes up on every change, and the view rebuilds only when that number or the sidebar choices change.
- **ID search:** the person table's search logic moved into `Population.idSearch()`. The table no longer needs to know how parcel IDs are stored.
- **Data points:** the list of what you can colour or filter by is now cached, not rebuilt on every lookup.

## Tests
They're in [app/test](app/test/), on a hand-built population of 8 people in 4 households. Run them with `cd app && npm test`; I added that line to the README. They cover:
- householder-first ordering and each person's role;
- data-point cases, drafts and swapping runs;
- ID and area search, CSV and summary;
- household colour rules, filters and fading;
- when the view rebuilds;
- opening and closing households;
- dot placement inside a circle.

The dot-placement test caught a real bug: in households of 8 or more, the outer people dots stuck out about 1% past the circle. That's fixed.

## Other changes
- `vitest` is a new dev dependency, and `app/test` is now included in `tsconfig.json` so the type check covers the tests.
- npm reported vulnerabilities in the installed packages during the install. I didn't look into them or run `npm audit fix`.
- I didn't change any Python, so I didn't rerun the 46 Python tests.

- Split PeopleLayer into Population (one run's people), PeopleView (choices,
